items.title: Iranian football team member granted asylum changes mind, will return to Iran
items.description: Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke says one of the seven members of the Iranian women's football delegation granted asylum in Australia now wants to be returned to Iran.

items.title: Live: Iran's police chief says protesters in the streets will be treated as 'the enemy'
items.description: The head of Iran's police has warned Iranians against taking to the streets to protest for regime change, saying their "finger is on the trigger". Follow live.

items.title: Dubai's 'tranquillity shattered' as Iran makes UAE a primary target
items.description: The United Arab Emirates is reporting more Iranian attacks than any other country as Tehran continues to retaliate against US and Israeli strikes.

items.title: Bets on Iran strikes paid millions but should gambling on war be allowed?
items.description: Gambling experts and US lawmakers have raised concerns about the ethics of online betting and whether insider information is being used to profit from war.

items.title: Live: Matt Canavan elected Nationals leader
items.description: The Nationals have elected Matt Canavan as their new leader, with Darren Chester elected deputy leader following the resignation of David Littleproud. Follow live.

items.title: New Nationals leader Canavan vows to 'fight back' for Australians
items.description: With a populist economic message, the new Nationals leader said local manufacturing and higher birth rates were key as he rejected the labels of "left" and "right" politics.

items.title: Foreign Facebook pages have been promoting One Nation. It wants them to stop
items.description: An ABC NEWS Verify investigation uncovers a raft of foreign Facebook accounts targeting Australian users. And they're just the tip of the iceberg.

items.title: Commercial rat baits to be banned from supermarket shelves
items.description: Rat baits could soon be restricted to licensed operators, after a change in regulations from the Australian Pesticides and Vetinary Medicines Authority.

items.title: NAPLAN resumes after technical issues paused online testing
items.description: NAPLAN testing for 1.3 million Australian school students resumes following technical problems that saw schools across the country unable to access the digital test.

items.title: Tony Burke to speak to AFP about right-wing attack on Muslims
items.description: The home affairs minister says he will discuss an alleged right-wing attack on a Muslim community in regional Victoria with the federal police.

items.title: Katie Perry wins High Court trademark case against Katy Perry
items.description: Australian fashion designer Katie Perry wins her High Court battle against international pop star Katy Perry in a long-running trademark case.

items.title: Live: Bundaberg flood extent may not be known for a week, but peak below expectations
items.description: Bundaberg is facing its worst flood in more than a decade, with the Burnett River peaking at about 7.4 metres. Follow live.

items.title: It could take 118 years to end racism at work, Gari Yala report finds
items.description: A landmark Indigenous-led report reveals that racism remains a daily reality for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander workers and, at the current rate of change, "it will take 118 years to eliminate racial slurs from Australian workplaces".

items.title: Two found corrupt over robodebt but Morrison cleared
items.description: Two people investigated over the so-called "Robodebt" scheme have been found to have engaged in serious corrupt conduct, while four others, including former prime minister Scott Morrison, have been cleared.

items.title: Live: NAB and Westpac economists forecast two rate hikes by May, ASX up
items.description: Westpac and the National Australia Bank have revised their earlier predictions to tip a rise in interest rates when the Reserve Bank of Australia meets next week. They are now forecasting that the RBA will lift rates by 25 basis points in March and May. Follow live.

items.title: Craig Freeman to stand trial over 1991 death of wife Melinda
items.description: Mr Freeman was charged last year for the murder of his then-wife, who was found dead in their home in Melbourne's north 30 years ago.

items.title: Quiz: Can you find your way around the world?
items.description: Where would you find the Frank Lloyd Wright marvel, Fallingwater? And what's the capital of Fiji?

items.title: 'Bloody glorious' farewell for beloved drag star Maxi Shield
items.description: A pair of purple stilettos sat atop her white casket while family and friends shared their favourite memories of her.

items.title: Docked boats, idle tractors: The Iran war fuel crisis is hurting Australia
items.description: Dozens of fishing trawlers have been stranded as a result of Australia's worsening fuel shortages, which some have described as the worst they have ever seen.

items.title: Police return to remote station in Gus Lamont search
items.description: SA Police have returned to the family's remote outback station as they continue their investigation into the disappearance of four-year-old Gus Lamont.

items.title: Two people drown at beach south of Wollongong
items.description: A man and a woman visiting from the UK have died after being pulled from the water at an unpatrolled beach in New South Wales.

items.title: Horsham man charged over triple-fatal crash on Western Highway near Ararat
items.description: Two Victorians and a South Australian man died in the crash involving five vehicles on the Western Highway near Ararat.

items.title: Daylesford crash inquest hears doctor has concerns for driver's memory
items.description: The diabetes doctor of the driver responsible for a 2023 collision in the Victorian town of Daylesford, that killed five people, tells a coronial inquest that he is "concerned" for his patient's memory.

items.title: UN determines Russian deportation of Ukrainian children are crimes against humanity
items.description: A UN investigation has found Russia's deportation and transfer of Ukrainian children since Moscow's full-scale invasion in 2022 amounts to crimes against humanity.

items.title: This outdated medical practice 'reflects very low respect for women'
items.description: Outdated medical devices are being used to perform a common obstetrics procedure on Australian women that can cause a condition known as Asherman's syndrome.
